key_insight: CalTennis is a much larger, real-world tennis video benchmark that makes it possible to test monocular-to-3D pose estimation under realistic game conditions. Its synchronized multi-camera setup and scale help reveal how well pose models actually generalize outside controlled lab settings.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of large, in-the-wild datasets for evaluating monocular-to-3D human pose estimation, especially with strong ground truth and synchronized multi-view video. Existing benchmarks are too small or too controlled to measure performance in realistic sports motion.
method: Collected over 11 million frames (51 hours) of tennis practice and match play from 40 players.
Captured each scene with 2-6 synchronized cameras at 60 Hz to enable multi-view 3D pose evaluation.
Built a benchmark designed specifically for monocular-to-3D pose estimation in real, unconstrained sports footage.
impact: CalTennis gives researchers a more realistic and much larger testbed for evaluating pose estimation models. This can improve model robustness, expose failure cases in the wild, and accelerate progress toward reliable 3D human motion understanding.
